detection.reason: Confirmed dark-pattern findings were recorded for nagging and forced action on the reviewed pages.

findings.title: Repeated third-party advertisement overlay
findings.why_this_matters: Repeated overlays can interrupt browsing and obstruct intended content after a user has dismissed promotional content.
findings.root_cause: Advertisement frequency and dismissal state are not sufficiently controlled.

findings.title: Bundled acceptance of terms at login
findings.why_this_matters: Bundled terms can make it difficult to distinguish conditions necessary for account access from terms relevant only to particular activity.
remediation_fix: Separate account-access terms from auction-specific terms.
findings.root_cause: Multiple agreements are presented as one condition of login.

evidence.summary: A third-party modal overlay obscures the vehicle listing page and reportedly reappeared after dismissal.

evidence.dom_snippet: By logging in, you agree with the User Agreement, Privacy Policy and Auction Terms.
evidence.summary: Login wording links account access with several terms without separate acceptance controls.

report.prepared_for: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Limited

assessment.scope_name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Web journey

executive_summary.overall_posture: The assessment identified potential dark-pattern concerns across reviewed digital journeys. The findings indicate areas where transparency, user choice and consent clarity may require further review.

priority_themes.summary: Terms and consent options may influence users to proceed without clearly separating essential requirements from optional permissions.
Loan-related interactions should provide clear information, meaningful choices and transparent consent mechanisms.

items.root_cause: Advertisement frequency and dismissal state are not sufficiently controlled.
items.corrective_action: Respect dismissal. Implement frequency caps. Maintain dismissal across navigation.

items.root_cause: Multiple agreements are presented as one condition of login.
items.corrective_action: Separate account-access terms from auction-specific terms. Explain applicability of each agreement. Provide separate controls where appropriate.

patterns.name: False Urgency
patterns.definition: Creating a false or misleading impression of urgency or scarcity to pressure an immediate decision.

patterns.name: Basket Sneaking
patterns.definition: Adding products, services, riders, add-ons or charges without the customer’s explicit consent.

patterns.name: Confirm Shaming
patterns.definition: Using guilt, shame, fear or emotionally loaded language to pressure a customer into accepting an option or avoiding an opt-out.

patterns.name: Forced Action
patterns.definition: Requiring a customer to complete unrelated actions or provide unnecessary information to access a product, service or basic functionality.

patterns.name: Subscription Trap
patterns.definition: Making cancellation, withdrawal, non-renewal or termination of a recurring service intentionally difficult, unclear or burdensome.

patterns.name: Interface Interference
patterns.definition: Manipulating visual design, presentation, hierarchy or defaults to favour an option that benefits the platform.

patterns.name: Bait and Switch
patterns.definition: Advertising a specific product, benefit or price but presenting a different, less favourable or higher-cost outcome later in the journey.

patterns.name: Drip Pricing
patterns.definition: Revealing mandatory charges, fees or unavoidable costs only late in a journey rather than presenting them upfront.

patterns.name: Disguised Advertisement
patterns.definition: Designing advertising or sponsored content to resemble neutral information, system messages or ordinary content.

patterns.name: Nagging
patterns.definition: Repeatedly interrupting or prompting a customer to take a particular action after they have declined, dismissed or deferred it.

patterns.name: Trick Wording
patterns.definition: Using confusing, vague, misleading or double-negative language that makes consequences of a choice difficult to understand.

patterns.name: SaaS Billing / Unsolicited Billing
patterns.definition: Charging a customer without clear, informed and transparent authorisation, including obscured recurring-payment or renewal terms.

patterns.name: Rogue Malware / Scareware
patterns.definition: Using fake security warnings, misleading alerts or deceptive pop-ups to pressure a customer into paying, downloading software or sharing credentials.

methodology.summary: Public-page review using captured screens, page text, observed interface behaviour and evidence-led classification.

limitations.statement: This assessment identifies potential findings from the reviewed public journey and is not a legal conclusion. Authenticated, payment, or other unassessed steps should be reviewed separately.
not_assessed_items: Long-term repeat behaviour beyond the tested session
